text:
rick (platform): Heads up — NimbusCo just reported consistent 90-120ms tail latency hitting our shared-hosted pool. They want a short-lived dedicated route pin so their canary can finish tests this afternoon. Thinking: temporary per-org pin to a small dedicated pool with TTL and audit log. Thoughts? :eyes:

maria (frontend): ok — we need a playbook: how the pin is applied, what header triggers it, UI surface to show pending pins, and an automatic rollback. also need a change record for audits.

sam (infra): Agree. Proposed implementation: header-based override. e.g. set X-Org-Routing: pool=nimbus-dedicated;ttl=3600;reason=test-canary

    ```yaml
    routing_overrides:
      - match: org_id == "nimbusco"
        action: route_to_pool
        pool: nimbus-dedicated
        ttl_seconds: 3600
        audit_event: route.pin
    ```

maria (frontend): that looks fine. console should surface TTL countdown and a one-click revoke. Add a checkbox "require manager approval" for >1h pins.

lena (security): security checklist: - ensure KMS-scoped keys for logs - no credential changes when pinned - require SSO approval for UI action. Also add an allowlist so only specific contacts can request pins.

sam (infra): note on quotas: routing to dedicated pool consumes reserved capacity. For short pins we can allow burst, but we should charge back to their org usage and flag if >10% of pool. Will add metric: routing.pin.peak_usage and tag with org_id.

ops-oncall: FYI — if pin is applied during business hours, page ops with the change request id.

rick (platform): operational flow I propose: 1) customer-request ticket -> ops reviews -> platform API creates route.pin with TTL -> console shows pin in "Active overrides" -> automation reverts after TTL or on manual revoke. Also create a fallback policy: if dedicated pool SLO degrades, auto-fallback to shared-hosted and mark incident.

maria (frontend): UI fields: org badge, pool name, TTL slider (15m/1h/6h/24h), reason, approver. show audit link -> event: route.pin/{id}. Add small warning: "This will direct production traffic to a reserved pool."

lena (security): add requirement: audit_event must include requestor email and ticket id. Logs stored for 1 year for enterprise customers.

sam (infra): implementation details for API: POST /internal/routing/pin { "org_id": "nimbusco", "pool": "nimbus-dedicated", "ttl": 3600, "requestor": "anna@nimbus.co", "ticket": "CS-1234" } returns pin_id and expires_at. Policy checks: membership in pin_allowlist, quota checks, pool capacity check.

deploy-bot: created change request CR-7891 for pin operation (author: rick). :white_check_mark:

rick (platform): who can approve? ops or product manager of that account. If >4h require two approvers. Also add automated tests in staging that simulate rollback.

maria (frontend): UX note — show a small timeline widget with pin history (applied, revoked, auto-expired) and link to logs.

sam (infra): telemetry: emit metric routing.pin_applied{org_id, pool, ttl} and a trace span routing.pin.apply to tie request to downstream latency. We'll add a dashboard tile and an alert if 95th exceeds baseline by 30%.

lena (security): also add a short retention policy for the payload: redact any PII in the reason field in logs.

ops-oncall: If this goes live, can we have a one-off runbook? quick steps: 1) revoke pin -> 2) monitor traffic shifting -> 3) if fallback fails, run emergency rollback to previous model version.

rick (platform): I'll draft the API spec and the console mock next. Plan: roll out to a small set of enterprise customers behind a feature flag. Sam will add quota/capacity checks. Lena will sign off on audit retention. Maria will add the UI. ops-oncall will vet runbook. Aim for internal rollout by EOW.

maria (frontend): copy. i'll add a mock and PR. :thumbsup:

sam (infra): i'll stub the API + metrics.

lena (security): will review.

ops-oncall: oncall acked.

rick (platform): thanks all. I'll post the PR link once it's up.

deploy-bot: PR #4127 created: feature/routing-pins. reviewers: maria, sam, lena.

maria (frontend): reviewing now.

sam (infra): quick question: do we want path-based match or only org_id header? My vote: org_id header for enterprise pins, path match for public debug routes.

rick (platform): org_id header only for enterprise. path-based is too brittle for customer long-term tests.

maria (frontend): agreed. done for now.
